text:
Maya: Quick thread on rollout metadata for model pinning. Mobile + server stubs persist pins and we end up with traffic stuck on retired variants. Need a schema that lets clients safely re-resolve or auto-migrate.

Priya: Can you show what clients are caching today?

Maya: Current minimal payload we return: `{"model":"redwood-7b","pin":"v2024-11-01","policy":"canary"}`. Clients persist the literal pin.

Ethan: Mobile persists the whole rollout response to avoid startup roundtrips. If the pin is immutable text we have to push config to force refresh.

Sam: Two approaches: add TTL on the pin, or add a deprecation signal + replacement pointer. TTL is simple; deprecation is explicit.

Maya: Sketches: TTL variant: `{"model":"redwood-7b","pin":"v2024-11-01","pin_ttl_s":86400}`. Deprecate variant: `{"model":"redwood-7b","pin":"v2024-11-01","deprecated_at":"2025-03-01T00:00:00Z","suggested_replacement":"v2025-02-12"}`.

Ethan: If we give suggested_replacement, we must also include a compatibility level because not all replacements are drop-in.

Sam: Propose `compat_level` enum: `backward-compatible | minor | breaking`. Clients decide auto-adopt rules.

Priya: Avoid unlimited freeform hints that SDKs rely on. Prefer a small set of namespaced hint keys and a schema_version.

Maya: Agreed. Top-level `schema_v` helps evolve fields. Also keep the rollout record compact; optional blob for advanced hints. Proposed minimal schema_v=1: `schema_v:"1", model:"redwood-7b", pin:"v2024-11-01", pin_ttl_s:"86400" (opt), deprecated_at:"..." (opt), suggested_replacement:"..." (opt), compat_level:"minor" (opt), client_hints:"..." (opt)`.

Priya: For SDKs, we should reserve `client_hints` keys (e.g., `refresh_endpoint`, `force_refresh_query`) and version them.

InfraBot: deploy-runner: schema_v=1 change staged to canary at 02:00 UTC.

Ethan: Server-side routing: if clients ignore suggested_replacement we should prefer non-deprecated variants at the edge, but keep original pin in logs for audit. Need telemetry to surface who still uses deprecated pins.

Sam: Server eviction policy idea: when `deprecated_at` < now and usage < threshold, progressively route to replacement; always emit events with original pin and resolved_model_id.

Maya: Telemetry plan: annotate request logs with `pin` and `resolved_model_id` and emit warning events when deprecated pins are used after `deprecated_at`. That allows targeted outreach.

Priya: Migration path: (1) Roll schema_v=1 with TTL + optional deprecate fields; (2) collect telemetry 30 days; (3) ship SDKs that prefer `suggested_replacement` when `compat_level` allows; (4) after 90 days, roll small-percent smart routing.

Ethan: For private/offline deployments, clients can't call home, so the pin record must include everything needed offline (TTL, replacement, compat). TTL is essential.

Sam: I'll draft a short RFC summarizing fields: `schema_v`, `pin`, `pin_ttl_s`, `deprecated_at`, `suggested_replacement`, `compat_level`, `reserved_client_hints`, plus server policy and migration timeline. Will include client behavior matrix for mobile/edge/server.

Maya: Please standardize duration naming: use `_s` suffix for seconds (e.g., `pin_ttl_s`).

Priya: :thumbsup: One last nit: keep enum naming consistent (`compat_level` vs `compat`).

InfraBot: deploy-runner: monitor deprecated_pin usage > 1% threshold during canary.

Maya: Action items: Sam RFC, telemetry keys, SDK guidance matrix. Ethan: add mobile note about persisted cache invalidation.

Sam: Filing RFC in #architecture by EOD.
